result.summary: Our patch contains the official fix's exact semantics — `relativePath.replace('\\','/')` before `split("/")` in `AbstractResource.forFile` (line 109), applied inline in the for-each instead of via reassignment; the only observable difference is the `relativePath` echoed in the "would go above root" IllegalStateException message (line 122), which is cosmetic. On top of that it adds a genuine defense-in-depth check in `ContextAssetRequestHandler.handleAssetRequest` (lines 55-65) that re-applies the `illegal` denylist to the *resolved* `resource.getPath()`. I verified this second check is effective and not fail-open: `AbstractResource`'s constructor strips the leading slash (line 62), so `forFile("folder/../WEB-INF/web.xml")` yields a ContextResource whose `getPath()` is `WEB-INF/web.xml`, which fully matches `^(((web|meta)-inf.*)|(.*\.tml$))` — closing a residual denylist bypass (raw path passes the pre-check, then resolves into WEB-INF, and `ChecksumPath.stream` offers no protection since a wrong checksum only triggers a redirect to the correct URL) that the official one-line fix leaves open. Main weakness is evidentiary, not semantic: the POV never reproduced before the patch and zero regression tests ran, so nothing here is empirically confirmed.
result.root_cause: `AbstractResource.forFile` canonicalized only on `/`, so on backslash-separated input a segment like `..\..\WEB-INF\web.xml` survived as one opaque term that escaped `..` collapsing and the WEB-INF denylist, reaching the context/filesystem still un-normalized.

dimensions.rationale: Backslash normalization lands at the shared sink exactly as the official fix does, and the handler additionally validates the post-resolution path, so both separator variants and dot-segment resolution into WEB-INF are closed.
dimensions.evidence: AbstractResource.java:109 `for (String term : relativePath.replace('\\', '/').split("/"))`; traced `folder\..\WEB-INF\web.xml` -> `folder/../WEB-INF/web.xml` -> terms [""],["",folder],[""],["",WEB-INF],... -> resource path `WEB-INF/web.xml` -> rejected at ContextAssetRequestHandler.java:62
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: Normalization is applied inside the final `forFile` method on AbstractResource — the single canonicalization point every Resource subclass and every asset handler funnels through — not at a caller or entry point.

dimensions.rationale: Correct normalize-then-check shape (validation runs on the resolved path, not raw input), which is the CWE-022 pattern, but containment is enforced by a WEB-INF/META-INF/.tml denylist rather than a base-dir allowlist, and there is no real-path/symlink canonicalization.

dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: No execution evidence supports the verdict: pov_before_reproduced=false (the POV never demonstrated the vulnerability pre-patch), pov_after_present=false, and regressions_ran=0. Both gates rest entirely on manual code tracing, not on the pipeline's results. The four added TestNG cases in ContextAssetRequestHandlerTest were never executed.

Containment is still a denylist ('^(web|meta)-inf.*' or '*.tml'), not a base-directory allowlist. It happens to be sound here because AbstractResource strips the leading slash and forFile emits no leading separator, but the check is coupled to that formatting invariant — any future change to path rendering in forFile/AbstractResource would silently make the re-check at ContextAssetRequestHandler.java:62 fail open rather than fail closed.
Dead branch: `resource == null` at ContextAssetRequestHandler.java:62 can never be true, since AbstractResource.forFile always returns createResource(...) (line 147). Harmless but misleading.

The explanatory comment at AbstractResource.java:104-108 is partly inaccurate — it claims the un-normalized segment reaches 'the filesystem largely unnormalized, which the underlying OS or servlet container may still interpret as real traversal', which understates the concrete pre-fix behavior (the whole `..\..\WEB-INF\web.xml` string becomes a single term appended verbatim to the resource path, escaping the context root on Windows).
